title: God’s Receptionist

description:
God’s Receptionist is a judgment-free space for women to pause in the middle of busy lives and reconnect with who they truly are in Christ. In a world that defines us by titles—mother, wife, professional, daughter—this podcast gently reminds us that before anything else, we are first a child of God.
This is not a place for perfection or expertise. Kristy is not a theologian, intellectual, or spiritual expert—she is simply a mom, wife, and woman of faith who has been where you are, or is walking through it right alongside you. This space exists not to teach from a pedestal, but to learn, grow, and seek God together as students of the Word.
Kristy shares spiritual lessons gathered from trusted faith leaders, cross-referenced with Scripture, and tested in the trenches of everyday life. Together, we explore who God is, what He has said, and how His truth shapes our identity.
Whether we’re diving into biblical foundations or having honest conversations about motherhood, marriage, womanhood, and life’s challenges, this podcast is a safe place for women of faith to grow spiritually without judgment. Here, we don’t just manage the “calls” of daily life—we learn to recognize the voice of the One who called us first.
What we explore together:
Biblical Foundations to anchor your faith
Identity Beyond Titles, reminding us we are daughters of the King
Honest Life Conversations rooted in grace, truth, and growth
Thank you for being here, for listening, and for choosing to grow closer to God alongside us. You are seen, you are welcome, and you belong here.

title: Pagan & Christian Creeds: Their Origin and Meaning
author: Edward Carpenter
description: In this work from 1921, Carpenter analyzes the origin of Christian beliefs, arguing that they are derived from pre-Christian myths and religions, rather than being new revelations to the human race. He believes that “psychologically man has evolved from simple consciousness to self-consciousness, and is now in process of evolution towards another and more extended kind of consciousness,” anticipating a post-Christian era. In the penultimate chapter, “The Exodus of Christianity,” he sets out his belief that for Christianity “to hold the field of Religion in the Western World is neither probable nor desirable.” Chapters such as “Solar Myths and Christian Festivals,” “Rites of Expiation and Redemption,” and “The Saviour-God and the Virgin-Mother” analyze his tenet as seen in different contexts. - Summary by Verla Viera

title: Bhagavad Gita

description: The content of the text is a conversation between Krishna and Arjuna taking place on the battlefield of Kurukshetra just prior to the start of a climactic war. Responding to Arjuna's confusion and moral dilemma, Krishna explains to Arjuna his duties as a warrior and Prince and elaborates on a number of different Yogic and Vedantic philosophies, with examples and analogies. This has led to the Gita often being described as a concise guide to Hindu philosophy and also as a practical, self-contained guide to life. During the discourse, Krishna reveals his identity as the Supreme Being Himself (Bhagavan), blessing Arjuna with an awe-inspiring glimpse of His divine absolute form. (Wikipedia)

title: Laotzu's Tao and Wu Wei (Tao Teh King)
author: Lao Tzu
description: The classic of the Way and of High Virtue is the Tao Teh Ching. Its author is generally held as a contemporary of Confucius, Lao Tzu, or Laozi. The exact date of the book's origin is disputed. The book is divided into two parts, the Upper Part and the Lower Part. The Upper Part consists of chapters 1-37, and each chapter begins with the word "Tao," or the Way. The Lower Part consists of chapters 38-81, and each chapter begins with the words "Shang Teh," or High Virtue. This 1919 edition names the Lower Part as the Wu Wei, or translated variously as "not doing," "non-ado," or "non-assertion." This edition also contains a history of the book and its author, Lao Tzu, along with a discussion of the Wu Wei. Lao Tzu's classic has been cherished as suggestions, rather than commandments, for finding one's path to beauty, goodness, and quality of life through a non-assertive understanding of the Way. (Summary by Melanie McCalmont)

It is a marvel of close translation, accurate and satisfactory. He has succeeded in doing exactly what he set out to do - to add nothing and to take nothing away, but to put into the typical quatrain, as determined by Fitzgerald and others, exactly what Omar and his unknown imitators said. (Summary by Algy Pug)This project was proof listened by Algy Pug and Bev J. Stevens.

title: Podcasting for Service Providers | Build Trust and Attract Clients Without Endless Content
author: Allison Nitsch | Podcast Strategist for Service Providers
description:
What if potential clients could hear how you think, understand your process, and trust your approach before they ever booked a sales call?
If you are a service provider who wants to use podcasting to build trust, attract clients, and market your business without becoming a full-time content creator, you are in the right place.
Podcasting for Service Providers explores how service-based business owners can use podcasting to help potential clients understand, trust, and choose them.
You may not need a podcast that publishes every week forever.
You need a strategic collection of episodes that communicates your best thinking, shows what makes your work different, answers the questions future clients are already asking, and gives people a reason to take the next step.
I’m Allison Nitsch, a podcast strategist and producer who has helped launch more than a dozen podcasts and has produced over 1,000 episodes for my own shows and my clients.
After years of working behind the scenes of ongoing podcasts, I began questioning the assumption that every business owner who wants the benefits of podcasting also wants the responsibility of creating new content every week. And as a service provider, you may not need that.
I believe your podcast should not become another endless obligation.
It should become an asset that keeps helping people discover your work, hear your perspective, understand your process, and decide whether you are the right person to help them.
On Podcasting for Service Providers, we will explore questions like:
-Do service providers really need a weekly podcast?
-How can a podcast help potential clients trust me before a sales call?
-What should I talk about if I want my podcast to support my services?
-How do I create episodes that showcase my expertise without giving random tips?
-How can I explain my process through podcast content?
-What questions should my podcast answer before someone hires me?
-How can I turn my ideas, stories, values, and client results into bingeable episodes?
-Should I start a traditional podcast, a private podcast, or a limited series?
-How many episodes does a podcast need to build trust?
-How can I use a podcast without becoming a full-time content creator?
-What makes a podcast bingeable?
-How can my podcast become part of my sales process?
-Can a podcast continue working for my business after I stop publishing?
-How do I create a podcast that helps listeners understand, trust, and choose me?
New episodes release every Wednesday and explore the strategy, messaging, structure, and possibilities behind creating a podcast that supports your business as a service provider and not one that takes it over.
Make sure you are following the show so you do not miss the next episode.
Next steps

Learn more about creating a Strategic Limited podcast series: https://allisonnitsch.com/series

title: You've Got People Problems
author: Melissa Ortiz, Talent Optimization Expert
description:
Let’s be honest. People problems aren’t just HR problems. They’re business problems.


They show up as missed goals, unclear accountability, hiring mistakes, disengaged teams, and leaders carrying more than they should. Over time, they slow growth, create frustration, and make running a business feel harder than it needs to be. And they aren’t solved by another policy, personality test, or quick fix.

Business would be simple… if it weren’t for people.


That’s the reality behind You’ve Got People Problems, a podcast focused on the human side of running a business. Each episode explores how leadership behavior, hiring decisions, role clarity, engagement, and organizational structure directly impact performance, culture, and results.


Through honest conversations with business owners, operators, HR leaders, EOS Implementers, and consultants, the show tackles real issues leaders face every day: why the “right hire” still isn’t working, how teams outgrow roles, when full-time isn’t the answer, why accountability breaks down, and what actually drives engagement beyond perks and pay.


This isn’t about HR checking a box or leadership theory. It’s about helping leaders slow down, recognize patterns earlier, and make more intentional people decisions that support both the business and the people inside it.


If you’re leading a team, building an organization, or trying to get out of the day-to-day firefighting that comes with people problems, this podcast is for you.

Subscribe, listen, and start making sense of the people side of your business.

title: Inside the Coaching Conversation: Coaching Demos and Debriefs for Coaches
author: Crystal Wagnner, PCC
description:
Have you ever listened to a coaching conversation and wondered why the coach chose that question?


Wish you could peek behind the scenes and understand what was happening in the moment?


Want to develop your coaching skills without simply being told what to do?

You're in the right place.


I'm Crystal Wagner, an ICF Professional Certified Coach (PCC), coach educator, mentor coach, coaching supervisor, and LEGO® Serious Play® facilitator. In each episode, you'll listen to a real coaching conversation, then we'll step back together to explore what happened, what I noticed, and how different coaching choices might have shaped the conversation.


At the beginning of each episode, I'll give you a little context about the client and invite you to listen for a specific moment in the conversation. After the coaching session, we'll debrief it together. I'll share what I was noticing, consider other coaching choices I could have made, and explore how those choices might have influenced the client's thinking and awareness.


You won't hear perfect coaching sessions—and that's intentional. Real coaching is messy, nuanced, and full of moments where several responses could have moved the conversation forward. Instead of striving for perfection, we'll explore the thinking behind the coaching so you can strengthen your judgment, expand your options, and grow in confidence.


Rather than giving you formulas to follow, my goal is to help you develop the reflective practice that allows you to trust yourself, listen more deeply, and discover your own authentic coaching voice.


Whether you're working toward an ICF credential, building confidence as a coach, or simply looking for thoughtful coaching demos, each episode will invite you to:

  • Notice the subtle moments that shape a coaching conversation.
  • Deepen your coaching presence and listening.
  • Strengthen your reflective practice.
  • Experiment with new approaches in your own coaching.
  • Discover multiple effective ways to coach the same moment.


Before we finish each episode, I'll leave you with a question to reflect on and a coaching experiment to try in your own conversations over the coming weeks.


If you're ready to learn from real coaching conversations, sharpen your coaching skills, and continue growing one conversation at a time, welcome to Inside the Coaching Conversation. I'm glad you're here.

title: That Salty Girl: Confidence, Reinvention, And Figuring Out What's Next
author: Holly Taylor: Navy Veteran, Entrepreneur, Mentor
description:
You don’t have to have it figured out to start.


After spending 26 years in the Navy, followed by a stretch in corporate America, Holly Taylor found herself starting over again in her 50s, this time, building a business from scratch. That business became The Salty Spray, a mobile spray-tanning company. If you’d told her at 18 that this would be her path, she probably wouldn’t have believed you. And that’s the whole point of this show.


When Holly retired from the Navy, the transition was harder than anyone had warned her it would be. What helped her through wasn’t advice or a perfect roadmap. It was hearing from people who had already been through it. People who reminded her that what she was feeling was normal. Now, she wants to be that person for you.


Most weeks, you’ll hear directly from Holly, talking to you the way she would talk to a friend at her kitchen table. No five-step formulas. Just honest conversations about starting over, rebuilding confidence, rediscovering your identity after a big change, and navigating that stuck, in-between feeling of not knowing what comes next.


Some weeks, she’ll introduce you to someone in the middle of a reinvention of their own; a client, a friend, or someone standing right where you might be now.


Through the women Holly tans in their own homes and the people who unexpectedly find their way into her DMs, she hears versions of the same story again and again. The woman ready to leave corporate for good and finally work for herself. The woman rebuilding her life after a divorce. Different ages. Different circumstances. But underneath it all is the same quiet question: Is it too late for me?


Holly’s answer is simple: it’s not.


You don’t need to have the entire path mapped out. You just have to be willing to take the next step before you feel ready.

Whatever’s next, you’re not behind.


Subscribe and listen to a new episodes every week. Also, join Holly’s newsletter, The Salty Scoop, for personal stories, photos, and pieces of life she doesn’t share anywhere else!

description: In the Dark, hosted by Madeleine Baran, is an award-winning investigative-journalism podcast that started in 2016. Season 2 examined the case of Curtis Flowers, who was tried six times for the same crime. In 2020, In the Dark released a special report on the coronavirus pandemic in the Mississippi Delta. In 2023, In the Dark joined The New Yorker and in 2024, it released “The Runaway Princesses,” a four-part series that asks why the women in Dubai’s royal family keep trying to run away. Season 3, released in 2024, asked why no one was punished for the killings of twenty-five civilians in Haditha, Iraq. In the Dark won the Pulitzer Prize for audio for Season 3. The podcast is a three-time Peabody Award winner and, in 2019, became the first podcast to win a George Polk Award, one of the top honors in journalism. title: History of the Revolutions in Europe

description: The View of the Revolutions of Europe by M. Koch, has been long known and highly esteemed on the Continent as a work of incontestable merit, and entitled to hold the first rank among productions of its kind. It occupied the labours and researches of thirty years of the author's life; and had the benefit of receiving, at different intervals, several additions and improvements from his own hand. As a concise, luminous, and accurate summary of general history, it stands unrivalled. The principal events and vicissitudes of more than fourteen hundred years are here condensed within an incredibly small space; bringing, as it were, under one view, the successive changes and destinies of Europe, from the fall of the Roman Empire, in the fifth century, to the restoration of the Bourbons in France. The countries which the different nations from time to time have occupied their laws and institutions-their progress from barbarism to refinement — the revival of arts and sciences — the origin of inventions and discoveries — and the wonderful revolutions, both moral and political, to which they gave birth,— are here detailed at once with brevity and perspicuity. The author has restricted himself as it were to the pure elements or essence of useful knowledge, discarding from his narrative everything that did not minister to solid instruction. His book has been compared to a sort of chart or genealogical tree of history, where only the grand and prominent events have been recorded, stript of all their secondary and subordinate circumstances, which often distract the attention without adding in the least to the interest or elucidation of the subject. His researches have thrown a new light on some of the difficulties and obscurities of the Middle Ages, particularly with regard to Chronology and Geography. His veracity and precision are unimpeachable; and, though his style has been thought inelegant, his candour, judgment, and erudition have never been called in question. - Summary by Andrew Crichton

title: Talking shit with Cdai
author: Courtney Ealy
description:
Talking Shit with Cdai is more than a podcast—it’s a chance to hear directly from someone who has lived through one of Chicago’s most well-known drill eras and who has spent years reflecting on the choices that shaped his life.

Born and raised around the Calumet Buildings on Chicago’s South Side before moving to Brick City, Cdai grew up alongside names like his brother Edai,  L’A Capone, RondoNumbaNine, Chief Keef, Lil Reese,Fredo Santana and many others who became part of Chicago’s drill history. As one of the original members of 600, he witnessed the rise of the movement, the success, and the devastating losses that defined that generation.

After being sentenced to decades in prison, Cdai has had years to reflect, mature, and develop a different perspective on life. This podcast isn’t about glorifying violence or reliving the past—it’s about honest conversations, accountability, growth, and speaking on real-life experiences from someone who has lived them.

Expect unfiltered discussions on music, sports, relationships, current events, prison life, street culture, and whatever else is worth talking about. Some episodes will feature call-ins from listeners, while others will include guests and open conversations with people from all walks of life.

The goal is simple: keep it real, make people think, have some laughs, and show that growth is possible. Your past may explain where you came from, but it doesn’t have to define where you’re going.

Welcome to Talking Shit with Cdai.

title: What to the Slave is the Fourth of July?
author: Frederick Douglass
description:
On July 5, 1852, Frederick Douglass delivered a powerful speech that shattered the illusion of American freedom and exposed the deep hypocrisy of a nation celebrating independence while millions remained enslaved. In "Fourth of July Speech," Douglass stands before a crowd of abolitionists and challenges them to confront the uncomfortable truth about liberty and justice. His words resonate with urgency as he argues that the Fourth of July is a day of mourning for the enslaved, not a celebration of freedom.

As Douglass recounts his own harrowing journey from enslavement to enlightenment, he raises profound questions about identity, humanity, and moral responsibility. He doesn’t just share his story; he ignites a fierce debate about the values upon which America was built. Listeners will experience the raw emotion and intellectual rigor that make this speech a cornerstone of American oratory.

This audiobook invites you to reflect on the ongoing struggle for equality and justice, urging you to consider what freedom truly means. With each word, Douglass challenges us to take a stand and fight against oppression in all its forms. Join this journey into the heart of America's moral conscience and discover why Douglass's message remains as relevant today as it was over 170 years ago.

As she dreams of a new existence abroad, Sam grapples with the unsettling reality that their paths may be diverging forever.

In this incisive exploration of love, ambition, and cultural clash, Sinclair Lewis delves into the complexities of a marriage tested by different desires and aspirations. Listeners will witness Sam's internal struggle as he confronts not only his wife's wishes but also his own identity and purpose in a rapidly changing world. With sharp wit and keen observation, Lewis exposes the societal expectations of the time, revealing the nuances of personal ambition against the backdrop of post-war Europe.

Will Sam and Fran find common ground, or will their diverging dreams lead to irrevocable change? Experience the emotional stakes and rich character development in 'Dodsworth,' a timeless tale that resonates with anyone who has ever grappled with the balance between love and self-fulfillment. title: Thoughts From My Thirties
author: Kala Riggins
description:
Life is complicated.
And honestly? Most of us are just trying to understand it while we’re still living it.
Thoughts From My Thirties is my ongoing conversation with the in-between seasons — the ones where you’re not who you used to be, but you’re not fully who you’re becoming yet.
I’m your host, Kala Riggins. I think out loud. I feel deeply. And I care about what’s underneath the surface.
Each episode is part reflection, part confession, part real-time processing. The kind of conversations that don’t try to tie everything into a bow… but help you breathe, soften, and realize you’re not behind — you’re human.
Because in your thirties, you stop chasing perfect and start craving honest.
You stop performing clarity and start asking better questions.
And you realize that most of life isn’t about having it figured out — it’s about staying present while you’re becoming.
No pressure.
No pretending.
Just permission to be in process.
Welcome to Thoughts From My Thirties.
This is where we think. We feel. We grow — in real time.

title: The Birth Pause
author: Chloe Campbell
description:
About The Birth Pause


Chloe searched for an existing podcast to share this story and couldn't find one that felt right. Most birth story podcasts offered long, linear play-by-plays from start to finish. What she wanted was something different — interview style conversations with the families she's attended, blending their lived experience with her clinical insight, told together, in each other's presence.


The Birth Pause explores birth not as a medical event but as a spiritual and personal transformation. Each episode asks not what happened, but what it did to you.


Hosted by Chloe Campbell — licensed midwife, founder of Supernatural Midwifery, and someone who has sat at the threshold with hundreds of families across New York City. This is not a play-by-play. This is the story underneath the story.

title: White Collar Crime: The Other Sentence
author: Lisa Mustard
description:
White Collar Crime: The Other Sentence is a podcast for families living through white collar crime, federal charges, sentencing, prison, incarceration, and the aftermath.
Hosted by Lisa Mustard, LMFT and coach, this show offers support for spouses, adult children, parents, siblings, and loved ones affected by a white-collar legal crisis. Lisa brings both professional experience and personal understanding to this topic as the daughter of a white-collar criminal.
When someone you love is accused, convicted, sentenced, or sent to prison, the legal case may belong to them, but the emotional fallout often reaches the whole family.
Each episode explores the private side of white collar crime: shock, shame, betrayal, isolation, parenting, marriage, money, reputation, public judgment, family relationships, and rebuilding after the life you knew changes.
This podcast is for the people who did not commit the crime but are still living through the consequences.
You didn't commit the crime. But you may still be living through the other sentence.
Educational and supportive content only. This podcast does not provide therapy, legal advice, or a substitute for working with your own attorney, therapist, or professional support team.

title: Reframe
author: Sarah Hill & Dani McCabe
description:
Welcome to Reframe — where honest conversations create new possibilities.


Are you feeling exhausted by the constant pressure to perform, be perfectly consistent, and constantly fix yourself? Welcome to a sanctuary away from the cultural matrix. We’re Sarah and Dani, and each week we sit down together to explore life, self growth, and everything in between.


As a psychotherapist (Dani) and an energetics and Human Design coach (Sarah), we spend our days holding space for others. But on this podcast, we turn the mirrors on ourselves. No scripts, no highly polished formulas, and absolutely no performance metrics. Just raw, unfiltered, and deeply messy real-life commentary from two expert minds figuring out their own human experience in real time.


From dissecting the dysregulation of mainstream social media to navigating rapid personal growth within long-term relationships—and even debating the perspective behind cold dishwater—we blend somatic wisdom, energetic blueprints, and psychological truth into a weekly permission slip for you to return to your ultimate inner authority.


We are evolving, changing, and here to share the spectrum of untold perspectives with you. If you are ready to broaden your awareness, challenge mainstream narratives, and finally feel less alone in the sticky middle of self-discovery, step into the room with us.
